messages:
maria: noticing a 3x p95 on region-us-east serving after yesterday's KV TTL tweak. hit-rate for prefix cache dropped from ~88% -> ~12% on a subset of shards. any ideas?
kevin: saw the alert, looking at tenant shard 42 which shows eviction spikes around 23:14 UTC.
sanjay: FYI infra-bot rolled out kv_ttl_scale=0.1 -> 0.01 for the 'latency-optim' experiment at 22:58 (can find rollout id).
ashley: wait that sounds like a huge TTL shrink, why was that pushed? :eyes:
infra-bot: deploy 2026-11-09T22:58:12Z by ci/cfg-applier — param kv_ttl_scale set to 0.01 in rollout rt-5932 (canary->global).
kevin: extracted perf profile from node g-12: kernel selection churn spiked — we fell back to the safe kernel more frequently after the eviction wave. that increases decode time by ~15% per token. sample: `kernel_select_fallbacks: 3.1k` in 5m window.
sanjay: TTL shrink caused earlier cache evictions which created high prefix cache churn; batching heuristics then queued tiny batches because KV miss latency bumped; combined effect drove kernel fallback heuristics to pick a slower path.
maria: do we have logs for batch size distribution? can we confirm micro-batches increased?
kevin: yes — batch histogram (5m): 
```
[0-16 tokens]: 74%
[17-64 tokens]: 18%
[65+ tokens]: 8%
```
previous baseline was ~40% small, 45% mid, 15% large.
ashley: small batches = more kernel dispatch overhead + worse kv pressure. that matches.
oncall: rolling back kv_ttl_scale to 0.1 on canary now. will monitor. :arrows_counterclockwise:
infra-bot: rollback triggered rt-5932-revert at 23:05:02Z, canary 2/2 healthy.
kevin: after rollback, hit-rate climbing back. eviction_rate on shard 42 dropped from 2400/s -> 90/s in 3m. kernel_fallbacks trend normalized, p95 returned close to baseline.
maria: thanks team. we should add a guard: disallow kv_ttl_scale < 0.05 without spike-sim check and perf signoff.
sanjay: also want a regression test that feeds a synthetic noisy-tenant to exercise prefix churn + batching. we missed the cascade path.
ashley: i'll file an infra ticket for the guard + add a perf-check to the deploy pipeline.
kevin: quick profiling note — pprof showed CPU hotspots in `kv::evict_loop` and `kernel_dispatch::select` during the incident; attaching snippet of flame (reduced):
```
kv::evict_loop 42%
kernel_dispatch::select 18%
decoder::step 12%
other 28%
```

sanjay: action items: 1) add TTL lower-bound guard (ashley) 2) add synthetic noisy-tenant perf test (sanjay) 3) add batch-size histogram to realtime console (kevin) 4) postmortem scheduled (maria).
maria: can we keep this thread for the postmortem notes? will update once we have pipeline PRs. :thumbsup:
kevin: one more — we should consider making kernel selection more resilient to transient KV misses by factoring in recent eviction_rate instead of only current miss latency. I'll prototype a smoothing window.
ashley: noted. creating infra ticket INC-4921 and linking here.
oncall: monitoring shows p95 back to baseline for canary and first 30% of rollout, keeping watch for 1h.
maria: thanks, everyone. great triage speed.
